descriptionChirho: All four clusters represent the same noun miqlat meaning 'refuge,' specifically the cities of refuge designated in the Torah for those who committed unintentional manslaughter. The clusters differ only in grammatical form: article (the refuge), possessive suffix (his refuge), construct state (refuge of), and prepositional prefix (for refuge). Multilingual evidence is perfectly uniform: Arabic uses malja' (مَلْجَأٍ/الْمَلْجَأِ/مَلْجَئِهِ) throughout; Spanish uses 'refugio' in all clusters; Korean uses dopicheo (도피처/도피) consistently; Hindi uses sharan (शरण) in all; Swahili uses makimbilio/kimbilio across all four. This is a single-sense technical legal term.
